ai.description: *Calliophis nigrescens* is a slender, 1m-long snake with a dark brown to black body and a bright red belly. It features a distinct white-spotted head and lacks the typical coral snake banding.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Calliophis nigrescens* is its uniform dark brown to blackish dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct, bright cross-bands found on other coral snakes.
ai.habitat: *Calliophis nigrescens* inhabits the moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Black Coral Snake is primarily nocturnal and secretive, often emerging at night to forage for small lizards and snakes among leaf litter and forest debris.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calliophis nigrescens* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calliophis nigrescens* is found in the Western Ghats of India, ranging from Maharashtra to Kerala, typically at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
